item.title: Implement rate limiter per SPEC.md in ratelimit.py
item.brief:
Operator request (authenticated, local socket): "Implement the rate limiter described in `SPEC.md` in `ratelimit.py` (the module currently only has stubs). Follow the spec exactly, including its error cases and edge cases; the tests in `test_ratelimit.py` only cover the basics. Keep it dependency-free (standard library only) and commit your work."

Acceptance criteria:
- Every behaviour, error case and edge case in SPEC.md is implemented exactly as written; where SPEC.md is silent on an edge case, do not invent behaviour, state the assumption in your summary.
- ratelimit.py uses only the Python standard library.
- Existing tests in test_ratelimit.py pass; add tests covering the spec's error cases and edge cases.
- Keep functions under 60 lines and follow the repository's existing style.
- Commit the work in the repository. Commit only as the configured git user, with no tool or AI attribution in the commit message.

state.summary:
Implemented TokenBucket and KeyedLimiter in ratelimit.py per SPEC.md, using only the standard library (time, collections), and added 16 tests to test_ratelimit.py. All 19 tests pass (the 3 original ones plus 16 new ones). Before the change, the 3 original tests errored on the NotImplementedError stubs.

A whole-change review failed on one blocking item: NaN max_keys passed the `< 1` check and only failed later as an AssertionError. The fix (`not max_keys >= 1`) and a NaN test are in commit 248b3d0. A delta review of that commit passed.

Assumptions where SPEC.md is silent: NaN capacity, refill_per_sec, max_keys and n are rejected as invalid. Non-integer max_keys (e.g. 2.5) is accepted, so the limit is effectively ceil(max_keys); this is not spec'd. Tokens are floats and wait_time returns (n - tokens) / refill_per_sec, so a caller sleeping exactly that long may hit a float rounding miss on the next try_acquire; no guard was added.

Left running: three reviewer `claude -p` processes (pids 388388, 392719, 394703) were started by the reviewer agents, not by me. I did not kill them; they stop when this run ends or can be stopped with kill <pid>. I started no servers.

Untracked __pycache__ was removed from the worktree; the tree is clean.

evidence.caption: Unit tests before the change (stubs) and after (spec implementation)

pr.body:
Approach: ratelimit.py holds TokenBucket (float tokens, refill computed from injected clock; no refill when clock goes backwards) and KeyedLimiter (OrderedDict of buckets; try_acquire and wait_time both move the key to MRU; the LRU key is evicted before inserting a new key beyond max_keys; invalid n is rejected before any key is created or evicted). Validation helpers use `not x > 0` / `not 0 < n <= capacity` so NaN is rejected. Tests: test_ratelimit.py adds error-case and edge-case tests (invalid params, bad n leaves state unchanged, clock regression, LRU eviction, wait_time counting as use, evicted key returns full, NaN max_keys).

Checks: python3 -m unittest test_ratelimit: 19 tests, OK. No linter or formatter is configured in the repo.

Assumptions: NaN is invalid input; non-integer max_keys is accepted (effective limit ceil(max_keys)); float rounding may make a try_acquire just after the wait_time delay fail.
pr.summary: Made per-key rate limiting possible with a stdlib-only token bucket. Now: TokenBucket (fractional refill capped at capacity, wait_time, clock regression safe) and KeyedLimiter (LRU-bounded per-key buckets). Before: stubs raising NotImplementedError; now: spec'd behaviour and ValueError validation, 19 passing tests.
pr.title: Implement token bucket and keyed rate limiter per SPEC.md

risk.why: New standard-library module behind no existing interface; no concurrency, persistence or API break. Behaviour changes only in the new module; tests added for error and edge cases. Whole-change reviewer rated medium; delta reviewer rated low for the one-line fix.
